trial_court: Additional District Judge, Panchkula, CR No.14323 of 2018
case_name: Tusharanshu Sharma Thru Gpa v. Nidhi Sharma Alias Nidhi Gupta
facts_of_case: Marriage between petitioner and respondent was solemnized on 14.04.2016 at Delhi and registered on 25.05.2016 at Panchkula. Petitioner filed petition under Section 13 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for dissolution of marriage. Respondent filed application under Section 24 of the Act which was withdrawn. Ex-parte order was passed against respondent on 27.09.2018.

legal_principles.principle: Proceeding ex-parte in a divorce case is not appropriate.
legal_principles.held: As the proceedings in present case are with regard to dissolution of marriage, it would not be appropriate that respondent-wife should be proceeded ex-parte.
cited_cases: Ramrameshwari Devi and others Vs. Nirmala Devi and others, (2011) 8 SCC 249
Bharat Rajpur Vs. Amrik Singh Aulakh, (2014) 56 RCR (Civil) 195

legal_principles.principle: Intentional delay in litigation is not evident.
legal_principles.held: From the perusal of the facts mentioned above, it is evident that the petition was filed in April 2017, respondent was served in August 2017 and replication by the petitioner-husband was filed in May 2018. The respondent-wife while moving the application for setting aside the ex-parte order, stated that she was busy in some other cases.

outcome.final_order: Order dated 03.12.2018 setting aside ex-parte proceedings order dated 27.09.2018 was quashed.
